criteria.text: The response identifies that the tax representations (SPA Section 4.12) are not included among the Fundamental Representations, so the tax representations and the pre-Closing Taxes indemnity expire nine months after Closing, before tax liabilities are likely to surface. It locates the issue in the Stock Purchase Agreement (the Fundamental Representations definition in Section 1.1 and/or the survival provision in Section 9.1), explains why this matters to Pisas, and recommends a fix.
hints: nine (9) months following the Closing Date

criteria.text: The response identifies that the Bill of Sale limits 'Retained Liabilities' to Salvage Business liabilities arising after the Transfer Time. As a result, pre-Closing Salvage Business liabilities, including the disclosed salvage-title class action, remain with the Company and fall outside the SPA's uncapped Retained Liabilities indemnity. It locates the issue in the Bill of Sale Section 1.3 and/or SPA Section 9.5(b)/9.2(c), explains why this matters to Pisas, and recommends a fix.
hints: to the extent arising after the Transfer Time

criteria.text: The response identifies that the Key Employee Agreement defines 'Business' more narrowly than the SPA, limited to in-person auctions at physical facilities, so the general manager's non-compete and non-solicit covenants do not cover the SimuLane online platform. It locates the issue in the Key Employee Agreement (Section 1.1 and/or Sections 7–8) and/or SPA Section 1.1/6.6, explains why this matters to Pisas, and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that the sale of the Company's stock is a Change of Control under the Key Employee Agreement that requires the general manager's prior written consent, and that the SPA does not address obtaining this consent. It locates the issue in Key Employee Agreement Section 5.3, explains why this matters to Pisas, and recommends a fix.
The response states that the SPA's general indemnity cap equals the Escrow Amount.
hints: cap equal to the Escrow Amount

criteria.text: The response states that the Escrow Amount is $3,600,000.
The response is formatted as a memo to the supervising partner that presents the issues separately.
For each issue it raises, the response gives both the document and the section where the issue appears.
The response claims that the tax representations (Section 4.12) are Fundamental Representations that survive until after the applicable statute of limitations.
The response claims that the Key Employee Agreement's non-competition covenant covers online auctions, including the SimuLane platform.
